papers.title: A Linear Parameter-Varying Framework for the Analysis of Time-Varying Optimization Algorithms

papers.title: Reachability-Augmented Dual Dynamic Programming for Optimal Path Parameterization
papers.summary: Optimal path parameterization (OPP) is a fundamental problem for planning trajectories along a prescribed geometric path under kinodynamic constraints and task-dependent objectives. Among existing OPP works, it remains challenging to simultaneously achieve feasibility guarantees, general-objective optimality certificates, and online-compatible computation in a unified framework, especially for third-order OPP (OPP3) with non-convex constraints. The key idea is to replace the relatively complete recourse assumption used in classical dual DP (DDP) with OPP-specific backward reachable sets, and then generate both value-function cuts and trial trajectories only inside these reachable sets. For convex and non-convex OPP, we prove global optimality and Karush-Kuhn-Tucker convergence of RDDP under OPP-specific conditions, respectively. Efficient instantiations are developed for second-order OPP (OPP2) and OPP3. Experiments show that RDDP achieves objective values comparable to convex-optimization baselines with speedups of approximately 15.3 and 4.9 times over the fastest of 4 tested solvers for OPP2 and OPP3, respectively. RDDP also achieves faster convergence than grid-based DP. Compared with reachability-analysis methods, RDDP retains the reachability mechanism while replacing local maximum-control propagation with value-function-guided control selection, thereby enabling objectives beyond traversal time. In summary, RDDP addresses a key capability gap in OPP by unifying certifiable general-objective optimization, reachability-based feasibility preservation, and online-compatible low-dimensional DP computation in a single framework.

papers.title: Data Center Load Reductions: Attribution, Measurement Limits, and Estimation
papers.summary: Hundreds of gigawatts of data center loads are seeking interconnection in the United States given the massive growth of artificial intelligence and cloud computing. In recent years, several incidents of data centers reducing their loads by hundreds to thousands of megawatts have been documented, raising grid reliability concerns. U.S. regulators have since ordered reliability standards for the integration of computational loads, and the North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) now calls on transmission owners to install disturbance recorders at these facilities to support root cause analysis. Such recorders usually observe only electrical quantities at the point of interconnection (POI). A sudden load reduction can be caused by a change in workload or a switch to backup supply. This work shows when POI measurements can distinguish the two mechanisms. It is established that they can produce identical POI voltage and current in a quasi-static constant power model, and during the transient their separation depends on the reduction relative to measurement noise, the clearing time, the dynamics through which workload reaches the POI, and the recorder bandwidth. When POI data are insufficient, an estimator that uses workload data is proposed to determine how much of the facility stayed connected. The results of this work identify the measurements and grid information utilities need to determine why data center load dropped.

papers.title: Physics-Guided Inferencer-in-the-Loop Digital-Twin for Real-Time Adaptive Emulation of Nonlinear PMSMs
papers.summary: A real-time digital-twin (RTDT) of a permanent magnet synchronous machine (PMSM) allows drive controllers to be tested in hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) before they meet the real machine. Its machine model rests on identified parameters or flux look-up tables (LUTs) from finite-element analysis (FEA) or characterization tests; the maps are regenerated offline when the machine changes, and online estimators track a few parameters such as resistance and PM flux. This article makes the executed model learnable from reference data. A physics-guided machine learning (PGML) network advances the currents and predicts torque in one step, trained with analytical one-step labels. In the proposed Inferencer-in-the-Loop (IIL) architecture, a GPU retrains the network while a field-programmable gate array (FPGA) executes the last accepted weights. For damper circuits, shifted parameters, and an FEA-calibrated saturated machine, one kernel form reaches average normalized mean absolute errors (NMAEs) of 0.19%-0.67% at measured FPGA kernel latencies of 0.30-0.34 $μ$s, and retraining for a shifted machine nears its final loss within 94 s. On a magnetically linear 200-W drive, a residual form corrects the analytical step and learns its physical parameters from operating data; each step takes under 2.5 $μ$s, 20 times faster than real time and ahead of the physical drive's measurements even at 20-kHz sampling. On six held-out runs (1193 s), its $i_q$ error is 5.9%-9.4% of measured RMS, against 10.4%-13.2% for an independently fitted grey-box model, and over 30 min of loaded heating its online-updated heads track a 4.1% winding-resistance rise with an RMS error of 0.44 m$Ω$.

papers.title: Passive Identification of Unequal Phase Grid Impedances by Phase-Domain Source Cancellation
papers.summary: Passive grid impedance estimators that return a single resistance--inductance pair cannot represent a grid whose phase impedances are unequal. This paper identifies a separate pair for each phase from recorded point-of-common-coupling (PCC) voltage and current without injected perturbations. In each phase, the unknown grid-source voltage is cancelled by a periodic difference (PD) or by a second-order-generalized-integrator notch difference (SOGID), and moving-window integration (MWI) replaces the current derivative by an integral and an endpoint feature. The resulting two-parameter regression requires a period or notch-frequency estimate but no phase-locked-loop angle. A voltage-balance analysis gives the source residual left by frequency mismatch and bounds the parameter error by the ratio of this residual to the conditioning of the two features. In the unequal-phase interval (8.3--9.8~s) of a 10-s EMTP grid-forming record, SOGID-MWI attains phase-averaged R/L errors of 5.09/0.33\%; a shared value has a minimum error of 41.67\% for the phase ratio 1:0.5:2. On a 50-s constant-impedance grid-following record, the errors are 0.56/0.06\% over the 20--30-s synchronization disturbance. In a controlled 40-dB noise study, a noise-referenced update rule reduces the white-noise GFL error from 55.9/65.0\% to 12.3/11.5\%.

papers.title: Safety of layered control systems via control barrier morphisms
papers.summary: Layered control architectures provide a powerful paradigm for synthesizing controllers for complex systems. Yet, translating guarantees at each layer to system-level guarantees is challenging due to the interactions between layers. To address this problem, this paper presents a categorical perspective on layered control architectures. Individual systems are represented as control coalgebras, their interactions are specified as morphisms to mediators, and system-level behaviors are obtained via composition defined categorically as a pullback. To analyze the safety of these systems, we formulate control barrier morphisms (CBMs), the categorical generalization of control barrier functions. We prove that feedback controllers satisfying a CBM condition render the associated safe subobject forward invariant. It is through CBMs that we can establish the safety of layered systems: given a CBM at each layer subject to compatibility conditions, the universal property of the pullback implies the existence of a CBM for the composed system. Safety of a full-order model being safety filtered by a reduced-order model is recovered as a specialization of the categorical framework.

papers.title: PyPSA-Libya: An Open-Source Energy System Model for National Decarbonization and Hydrogen Export Pathways
papers.summary: Libya possesses significant renewable energy potential that remains largely untapped. This paper presents PyPSA-Libya, a national-scale model built on the PyPSA-Earth framework, designed to explore optimal transition pathways for the Libyan power sector. We present two primary studies: (1) an electricity-only capacity expansion analysis comparing a zero-emission constraint against an unconstrained baseline at 36-cluster resolution, and (2) a sector-coupled hydrogen export study evaluating the levelized cost of exporting 70 TWh/year of hydrogen to Europe under three technological scenarios and a 100 EUR/tonne CO2 carbon tax regime. Results indicate that while solar PV dominates the domestic capacity mix, integration of hydrogen production significantly alters grid storage requirements. Furthermore, under carbon pricing, steam methane reforming with carbon capture (SMR-CC) frequently out-competes pure green electrolysis, establishing a lower-cost compliance pathway for cross-border export. The model, data, and configuration files are released under an open-source license to support transparent energy planning in Libya.

papers.title: State-Dependent Delay Modeling of Wind-Farm Wake Dynamics
papers.summary: Turbines convert wind to electrical power. In the wake of a turbine, wind speed is reduced in proportion to the amount of power extracted. In a wind farm, downstream turbines may be located in wake of an upstream turbine, requiring coordination to yield maximum power generation. This paper creates a state-dependent delay model for a two turbine wind farm. The upstream turbine creates a wake that diminishes the wind speed at the downstream turbine. Changing the upstream turbine operation will affect the downstream turbine after a delay that depends on the wind-propagation time between them. This delay depends on the upstream power extraction and it can destabilize the combined dynamics. Conventional models of this effect rely on nonlinear partial differential equations (PDEs). Control design and analysis with such models is difficult with established methods. We first show that the PDE model can be represented by an Abel-type state-dependent delay differential equation. The equation has an implicit solution. To obtain an explicit representation, we then introduce a simplified state-dependent delay model. Both models predict destabilizing interactions between the two turbines. Numerical examples illustrate delay-induced oscillations using the simplified model and verify their effectiveness in simulation.

papers.title: Trajectory-Planning Attitude Control System for Satellites with Magnetic Attitude Control and One Reaction Wheel
papers.summary: Selecting attitude actuators for spacecraft in low earth orbit (LEO) often involves a trade between reaction wheels and magnetorquers. papers.title: Data-driven Wasserstein distributionally robust generalized Nash equilibrium problems with heterogeneous uncertainty
papers.summary: We study stochastic generalized Nash equilibrium (GNE) problems with heterogeneous, stochastic uncertainty in the cost functions. To address the distributional uncertainty, we let each agent construct an individual Wasserstein ambiguity set around an empirical distribution obtained from private data. We establish finite-sample robustness guarantees for any distributionally robust (DR) GNE. Focusing on variational equilibria, we derive a DR variational inequality (VI) reformulation and establish asymptotic consistency with the nominal stochastic game. Under mild conditions, we derive an exact finite-dimensional generalized Nash equilibrium reformulation. We then quantify how heterogeneous worst-case distributions affect monotonicity, and derive conditions for uniqueness and equilibrium sensitivity. To compute a variational DR GNE, we propose an inexact projected method and establish convergence under vanishing oracle errors, an asymptotic error bound under bounded oracle errors, and linear convergence under exact oracle evaluations.

papers.title: Response time central-limit and failure rate estimation for stationary periodic rate monotonic real-time systems
papers.summary: Real-time systems consist of a set of tasks, a scheduling policy, and a system architecture, all constrained by timing requirements. Many everyday embedded systems, within devices such as airplanes, cars, trains, and spatial probes, operate as real-time systems. To ensure safe failure rates, response times-the time required for the exection of a task-must be bounded. Rate Monotonic real-time systems prioritize tasks according to their arrival rate. This paper focuses on the use of the central limit of response times built in \cite{zagalo2022} and an approximation of their distribution with an inverse Gaussian mixture distribution. The distribution parameters and their associated failure rates are estimated through a suitable re-parameterization of the inverse Gaussian distribution and an adapted Expectation-Maximization algorithm. Extensive simulations demonstrate that the method is well-suited for the approximation of failure rates. We discuss the extension of such method to a chi-squared independence test adapted to real-time systems.

papers.title: A Community Impact-Centered Network Reduction Method for Power Systems Resilience Planning
papers.summary: Power systems resilience planning requires evaluating many hazard scenarios and investment portfolios, often requiring network reduction for computational tractability. The resulting aggregation, however, can obscure community impact data needed for equitable planning. We present a network reduction method that jointly preserves network physics and the spatial distribution of community data. We embed a household-level scarce resource score that characterizes outage impact within optimization-based Kron reductions with two formulations: a scarcity-weighted method that prioritizes vulnerable nodes, and a scarcity-constrained method that bounds data dissimilarity within aggregated clusters. The scarcity-constrained method performs best, achieving 86% reduction with worst-case voltage errors below 0.01p.u. while preserving the spatial distribution of community data. By explicitly controlling data heterogeneity within and across clusters, the proposed method yields reduced networks that retain decision-relevant community information without sacrificing electrical accuracy.

papers.title: Input Design for Angles-Only Initial Relative Orbit Determination Using Active Learning
papers.summary: Angles-only initial relative orbit determination (IROD) is a challenging estimation problem, as the lack of direct range information results in scale ambiguity and weak practical observability. papers.title: Revisiting Certainty Equivalence: The Structural Coupling Between Estimation and Control in Underactuated Nonlinear Systems
papers.summary: The certainty equivalence (CE) principle underpins a wide range of control architectures by enabling the separation of estimation and control design. While this property holds for linear systems, its validity in nonlinear settings remains limited and often implicitly assumed. This paper revisits CE from a nonlinear perspective, showing that estimated states induce an intrinsic coupling between estimation and tracking dynamics. By analyzing the closed-loop system in tracking-error coordinates, we demonstrate that nonlinear state dependence gives rise to higher-order interaction terms during aggressive transients. Motivated by this limitation, we propose an estimation-aware (EA) control paradigm that incorporates estimation quality into the feedback law to isolate estimation-induced loops. The formulation remains filtering-agnostic while preserving general applicability to smooth, underactuated nonlinear systems. We derive analytical conditions guaranteeing bounded tracking under uncertainty, validating the framework under high-fidelity quadrotor flight simulation along complex 3D trajectories at speeds up to 57.6 km/h. Frequency-domain evaluations demonstrate that the EA law extends tracking bandwidth by 39% and improves stability margins by up to 55%, effectively mitigating severe cross-couplings to offer a robust alternative to classical CE-based designs.

papers.title: Coordinated and Uncoordinated Channel Tracking for High-Rate IoT in Distributed Massive MIMO With Low-Resolution ADCs
papers.summary: This paper investigates dynamic channel tracking for high-rate Internet of things (IoT) in distributed massive multiple-input multiple-output (mMIMO) with low-resolution analog-to-digital converters (ADCs), where pilot and data activities are decoupled, pilots are reused, and mobile channels evolve across access slots. papers.title: Stochastic MPC under Heavy-Tailed Disturbances: An Extreme Value Theory Approach
papers.summary: Safety-critical control systems must contend with disturbances whose extreme deviations occur far more frequently than classical light-tailed models predict. Existing stochastic MPC (SMPC) formulations tighten constraints using an assumed distribution, a moment bound, or a finite scenario sample, each of which degrades under an unknown heavy-tailed disturbance. This paper develops an SMPC formulation for linear systems under heavy-tailed disturbances that is only assumed to be regularly varying, which allows an explicit extreme value theory (EVT) characterization of the tube error tail that is asymptotically exact. We further show that closed-loop dynamics induce temporal clustering of rare excursions across the prediction horizon, and characterize this clustering through a closed-form extremal index estimable from data. The resulting clustering-corrected constraint bounds the probability of a rare-event episode over the horizon, rather than only the marginal per-step exceedance probability. Simulations of a linear two-CSTR-in-series process and of a nonlinear unicycle navigating past an obstacle under Student-$t$ disturbances validate both approaches and demonstrate reduced frequencies of safety constraint violations.

papers.title: Smoothing the Ramp, Not the Peak: Scheduling-Induced Power Dynamics of LLM Inference and Their Grid-Scale Consequences
papers.summary: Large language model inference serving is a fast-growing electricity load whose power dynamics remain uncharacterized from a grid-planning perspective. Using real, measured GPU power traces, we show that chunked prefill scheduling, a latency-motivated technique already deployed by default in production LLM serving, is a controllable knob that regulates power ramp rate without touching peak power. Contrary to the intuitive hypothesis that splitting a long prompt's computation into smaller steps should flatten its power spike, peak power stays relatively the same while mean ramp rate falls substantially. Critically, this ramp-rate benefit is not a fixed property of the policy: it grows monotonically with system saturation, and we confirm this along two independent axes: concurrency and long-prompt request load (from near zero at low whale incidence to 39.6% at high whale fraction/size). We translate this single-GPU mechanism into an operational grid quantity, regulation-reserve procurement, posed and solved as a chance-constrained problem using a model-free bootstrap directly resampling real measured power traces. For independently operating servers, chunked prefill reduces the fast-ramping reserve requirement by an estimated 24% at heavy load (95% CIs within 13-34%) and 12% at moderate load, consistently across reliability levels from 95% to 99.9%. Repeated with 100 trials per policy on two-GPU tensor-parallel deployments, the reduction is about 36% for a dense 14B model and 10% for a sparse mixture-of-experts model. The benefit holds for ramps resolved at up to 2 s and persists at a reduced 16-20% when servers' load changes are synchronized. Together, these results identify a no-cost lever for fast-timescale demand shaping that is available today, whose benefit is largest when data centers run hottest.

papers.title: Joint Antenna Positioning and Pilot Power Allocation for Uplink Fluid Antenna-Aided Cell-Free Massive MIMO Systems
papers.summary: This paper investigates joint fluid antenna (FA) position optimization and pilot power allocation for uplink cell-free massive MIMO networks supporting ultra-reliable low-latency communication (URLLC) traffic under pilot contamination. This mapping translates complex latency requirements into explicit NMSE thresholds, maintaining a median absolute approximation error below 0.03 dB and less than 10% relative error for over 90% of practical-regime samples. Given the nonconvex nature of the formulation, we propose an alternating optimization framework. Antenna positions are iteratively updated via successive convex approximation using analytical gradients and closed-form Euclidean projections. Furthermore, we introduce an auto-calibrated regularization variant to navigate the Pareto frontier between estimation accuracy and energy consumption. Numerical results show the proposed positioning yields up to 22% NMSE improvement over fixed uniform arrays while operating 7-8x faster than particle swarm optimization. The power allocation achieves within 0.5% of the global optimum at over two orders of magnitude lower computational cost, providing up to 39% pilot energy reduction with negligible estimation penalty.

papers.title: A New Parametric Uncertainty Approach to Systems with Time-Varying Delay and Feedback Stabilization

papers.title: Repeated Binary Direct Collinear Impacts Under Incremental Contact Laws With Residual Indentation: A Hybrid Systems Formulation
papers.summary: Incremental contact laws specify the normal contact force through a differential relation, possibly carrying an internal state, driven by the indentation and its rate. In some, the force is extinguished at a nonzero indentation, whether by plastic deformation or by an elastic aftereffect, so that a residual deformation remains at separation. Such laws sit uneasily within rigid body dynamics, which admits no deformation. The tension is tolerable when the indentation is small relative to the bodies, so that it may be carried constitutively rather than geometrically. Even then, the contact law alone does not determine the interaction of the bodies. Because force and indentation no longer vanish together, conditions for the commencement and termination of contact must be supplied separately. So must the fate of the deformation and internal state at separation, neither of which the equations of motion contain. This article formulates the repeated direct collinear impact of two convex bodies under external forces as a hybrid dynamical system. The contact interface is modeled as a massless element carrying the contact law and its state, coupled to the bodies through relative velocity and an interaction force dictated by the contact state. Consequently, all switching and resets are confined to the interface, leaving the geometry and the equations of motion of the bodies unaltered. The principal analytical properties of the resulting formulations are established, among them passivity and completeness; the branching of solutions at the onset and termination of contact is also examined. The framework is demonstrated through numerical simulations.

The deployed planner therefore avoids the iterative classifier-free denoising loop and VAE decoding required for future-video synthesis, while dynamically allocating backbone depth according to trajectory quality. On NAVSIM, the adaptive single-trajectory planner achieves 90.8 PDMS; a separate fixed-exit variant reaches 92.6 PDMS with 64 proposals. It further obtains 89.9 EPDMS on NAVSIM v2, yielding the best reported results among the compared front-view video world-model planners. Without target-domain fine-tuning, Adaptive-WAM transfers to nuScenes with 0.88 m average L2 error and a 0.08\% collision rate. On an A100, adaptive routing improves PDMS from 90.62 to 90.79 while averaging 170 ms end-to-end planning latency, approximately 10\% below the 190 ms fixed block-15 planner and 47\% below the 320 ms fixed full-depth planner. papers.title: Mechanistic Interpretability for End-to-End Self-Driving
papers.summary: End-to-end (E2E) autonomous driving models achieve strong planning performance but remain largely opaque, limiting observability and trust. We apply mechanistic interpretability to E2E driving by training Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) on the internal activations of a simple, single-camera end-to-end path planning model. Unsupervised clustering of SAE latents reveals interpretable structure aligned with route intent, vehicle speed, and braking behavior, recovering route intent with 98.3% accuracy without supervision. Through paired counterfactual image edits, we further show that specific SAE features are visually grounded and systematically respond to scene changes such as traffic light state and stop sign presence. Steering individual SAE latents produces predictable, monotonic changes in planner outputs including lateral displacement, curvature, and braking. Finally, we demonstrate a practical application of these representations: we build a lightweight adapter trained on SAE latents that reduces trajectory selection error by 3.44%, outperforming an equivalent adapter that omits SAE latents, confirming that the sparse representation captures useful information for interpretability. papers.title: Aligned Delta-Triplane Transformers as Occupancy World Models
papers.summary: Occupancy World Models (OWMs) aim to predict future 3D occupancy scenes from historical observations and future ego motions, providing a useful world simulation tool for autonomous driving. Existing methods usually rely on large networks to implicitly align multi-frame historical states and predict future occupancy in a full-state manner, which is costly and redundant because most scene regions remain unchanged over short time intervals. In this paper, we propose Aligned Delta-Triplane Transformer (ADTT), a compact 4D OWM that explicitly aligns historical triplanes with ego-motion compensation and predicts only future scene changes. Based on the aligned triplane prior, a query-conditioned Transformer predicts residual changes, where ego-motion queries guide controllable future motion and learnable external queries capture scene changes beyond ego motion. The predicted changes are added to the aligned prior and decoded into future occupancy scenes. Experiments on Occ3D-nus show that ADTT achieves state-of-the-art forecasting performance with fewer parameters and higher FPS. Our code is publicly available online: https://github.com/kyoran/ADTT.

papers.title: NTR: Neural Token Reconstruction for Scene Token Bottleneck in End-to-End Driving
papers.summary: Recent perception-free end-to-end (E2E) autonomous driving methods bypass explicit perception outputs by compressing dense image patch tokens into compact scene tokens for downstream trajectory generation and scoring. While these scene tokens form a compact visual bottleneck for the planner, they receive supervision solely from the planning objective, providing limited constraints on the encoded visual information. To address this limitation, we introduce Neural Token Reconstruction (NTR), a representation learning framework to directly constrain the compact scene-token bottleneck in perception-free driving. NTR introduces a self-distillation masked latent reconstruction objective that reconstructs masked patch-level latent features using only compact scene tokens as reconstruction memory. This forces reconstruction gradients to pass exclusively through the scene-token bottleneck, encouraging scene tokens to preserve richer and less redundant visual representations for planning. We further introduce semantic priors derived from foundation-model annotations as a weak semantic interface biasing reconstruction targets toward driving-related structures without introducing explicit perception heads. All auxiliary reconstruction components are removed at inference time, leaving the deployed planner unchanged. NTR achieves state-of-the-art performance on three public autonomous driving benchmarks, including 8.0461 RFS on Waymo E2E and 94.1 PDMS / 90.9 EPDMS on NavSim1&2. The learned scene tokens exhibit lower pairwise redundancy and higher effective rank, indicating that effective bottleneck supervision improves both compact visual representation learning and planning performance.

papers.title: Lexicographic Descent: A Gradient-Based Approach to Optimize Totally Ordered Rulebooks via Parametric Scalarization
papers.summary: Safety-critical systems, such as autonomous vehicles, must satisfy conflicting constraints and objectives, collectively called rules, typically ordered lexicographically. Preemptive lexicographic optimization solves a sequence of problems, one per priority level. However, higher levels are optimized without considering lower ones, making the approach susceptible to suboptimal solutions. On the other hand, scalarization optimizes all levels jointly and so avoids this myopia, but a finite weighted sum permits trade-offs across priority levels, and exact scalar representations lack the regularity standard solvers require. We propose Lexicographic Descent, which combines the benefits of both: a single weighted sum whose relative weights decay at priority-dependent rates, recovering the lexicographic order in the limit. We show that Lexicographic Descent converges to constrained stationary points of the highest-priority rule, matching preemptive guarantees. Since the lower-priority weights vanish, we derive a necessary condition for the lower-priority rules to keep guiding the iterates, with the aim of avoiding suboptimal stationary points of the higher-priority rules. We show that Lexicographic Descent can exploit problem structure to reach the lexicographic optima, and outperforms the preemptive approach on an autonomous driving case study.

papers.title: FastBEVFusion: Simple Multi-Modal Fusion for 3D Object Detection at 50 FPS
papers.summary: Reliable real-time 3D object detection based on LiDAR and camera data is critical for safety in autonomous driving, where systems must accurately perceive their surroundings with minimal latency. Many state-of-the-art systems achieve high-quality detection results but fail to meet real-time constraints, limiting their practical use. To address this challenge, we propose FastBEVFusion, a simple, fast, and robust fusion system for 3D object detection. Based on modality-specific features, FastBEVFusion projects these features into semi-aligned modality-specific BEV spaces, without relying on a computationally intensive and potentially error-prone depth estimation. Given these BEV spaces, we propose a light-weight, soft, and dynamic fusion module based on cross-attention, which adapts dynamically to the scene context and enables feature fusion across the entire BEV spaces. Experiments on the complex nuScenes dataset show that FastBEVFusion outperforms state-of-the-art real-time systems, and achieves over 50 FPS without deployment libraries. Additionally, our system shows strong robustness to calibration errors, making FastBEVFusion a powerful 3D object detection system for real-world applications.

papers.title: OSWAM: An Effective World Action Model with One-Step Action Generation
papers.summary: Direct-policy World Action Models (WAM) have demonstrated the benefits of decoupling action generation from explicit future visual prediction for efficient inference in autonomous driving and embodied control. However, they still require tens of denoising steps to achieve competitive action quality, incurring substantial latency and hindering real-time deployment. Simply reducing the number of denoising steps will collapse the nonlinear multi-step denoising trajectory into coarse updates, substantially degrading action quality. To reduce the denoising steps while enabling real-time action generation, we present an effective world action model with one-step action generation, namely OSWAM, for autonomous driving and embodied control. We argue that it is the absence of structured action priors in random noise initialization that forces direct-policy WAMs to recover coherent action sequences through iterative denoising. Hence, we construct imagination tokens to initialize the diffusion process, providing physical priors and action-conditioned representations. We further introduce privileged information distillation with future conditioning to enhance future-aware action generation. As a result, OSWAM can efficiently and effectively generate high quality actions in just one diffusion step. Our experiments demonstrate that OSWAM achieves comparable or even better results in both autonomous driving and embodied control than direct-policy WAM and Joint-WAM that require tens of steps. It obtains approximately $3\times$ speedup over direct-policy WAM baselines and supports real-time compiled inference with latency as low as 40ms on an NVIDIA RTX 5090 GPU. The project page is available at https://gwenzhang.github.io/OSWAM/

papers.title: Hyperparameter and Neural Architecture Search via Evolutionary Optimization for Reinforcement Learning: HPNAS-RL
papers.summary: In this study, we propose a dual-branch evolutionary framework that simultaneously performs Neural Architecture Search (NAS) and Hyperparameter Optimization (HPO) for Reinforcement Learning (RL) in Autonomous Driving (AD) tasks. While NAS has shown strong potential in automating architecture design for Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), its application to RL remains limited, especially in scenarios that require joint optimization of architectural and training dynamics. Building on our prior work on Evolutionary Multi-Objective NAS (EMNAS), the proposed framework evolves discrete network architectures and continuous hyperparameters in parallel under a unified multi-objective search strategy. In this setup, NAS targets the convolutional layers of the RL policy network - responsible for visual feature extraction, while HPO focuses on optimizing critical RL hyperparameters. To accelerate convergence and improve generalization, we incorporate parallel evaluation and a teacher-student policy transfer mechanism. Experiments in a high-fidelity driving simulator show that the joint NAS-HPO framework consistently outperforms standalone NAS, yielding policies with higher rewards, fewer parameters, and improved stability. These results highlight the benefits of jointly optimizing model structure and training dynamics for scalable and effective RL agent design.

papers.title: Towards AI-Assisted Clinical Trial Matching: Practical Considerations, Multicenter Evaluation, and Real-World Deployment
papers.summary: Clinical trials are essential for evidence-based medicine and drug development, but many fail because of insufficient patient enrollment. Although there is growing interest in using AI to support patient recruitment, existing systems largely perform eligibility assessment alone and have rarely been evaluated in real-world workflows. Here we present TrialGPT 2.0, an AI-assisted clinical trial recommendation system improved for responsible real-world deployment. Rather than asking only whether a patient may qualify, the system assesses which trials warrant further consideration given the patient's current clinical needs and local workflow priorities, and provides structured, inspectable explanations for expert review. Importantly, we evaluated TrialGPT 2.0 retrospectively and prospectively across government research, patient-advocacy, academic medical center, and community-based radiation-oncology settings. In retrospective multicenter cohorts comprising 288 cases, TrialGPT 2.0 retrieved at least one clinician-recommended trial in its top 10 recommendations for approximately 91% of cases while reducing clinician screening time by 55.0%. In a six-month prospective evaluation embedded in an active precision oncology tumor board, TrialGPT 2.0 contributed additional trial opportunities missed by the routine workflow, increasing the number of patient cases with at least one final trial recommendation by 90.9%. To support scientific reproducibility, we also developed NIH-TrialBench, a clinician-authored benchmark comprising 126 diverse synthetic patient vignettes and matching scenarios from 11 NIH Institutes and Centers. Together, these findings support the value of AI to assist clinical trial matching by improving clinician efficiency and identifying frequently overlooked trial opportunities, ultimately helping to expand and accelerate accrual to cancer trials.

papers.title: Fair Recommender Systems for Intersecting Groups
papers.summary: Recommendation systems that optimize for the average user can fail to capture the preferences of diverse demographic groups. We consider a dynamic recommendation system, where arriving users can belong to different demographic groups. Importantly, these groups can intersect, and a user may belong to several groups. We first show that over time, any group-blind policy (which excludes all current-user group information) recommending $K \geq 1$ items incurs linear total regret under mild conditions. In turn, we introduce three group-aware algorithms based on the classical Upper Confidence Bound algorithm (UCB): i) Intersection-Fitting, which runs UCB on each intersection, but has a sublinear group- and intersection-level regret guarantee with an exponential dependence in the number of groups; and ii) two group-level heuristics, Inner-Outer UCB and Group-Item UCB which allocate different arms to different groups, and use a sleeping expert meta-learner to choose which active group's recommendation an intersection should inherit at any given time step. We provide experimental results on two datasets, Goodreads and BoardGameGeek, and highlight that our heuristics can be preferable to the intersection-fitting algorithm when intersection-level preferences are closely related to group-level preferences, but that intersection-fitting performs better when different intersections within a same group prefer different items.

papers.title: TACFormer: Transformer-Based Generative Model for Target-Conditioned De Novo PROTAC Design
papers.summary: Targeted protein degradation (TPD) represents a fundamental shift in drug discovery, moving beyond traditional target inhibition toward the event-driven removal of disease-causing proteins. A prominent strategy for TPD is the use of proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs), heterobifunctional molecules that selectively route a protein of interest (POI) to the ubiquitin-proteasome system for degradation. While PROTAC design still relies heavily on trial-and-error synthesis and experimental testing, deep generative models offer a promising means to explore PROTAC chemical space in silico and generate novel molecules. However, many existing generative methods formulate PROTAC design primarily as a linker-generation problem, with POI-binding (warhead) and E3-ligase-binding components fixed in advance. This restricts exploration of the full PROTAC chemical space and often leaves the POI implicit through the predefined warhead, rather than using protein-level information as an explicit conditioning signal during generation. To address these limitations, we propose TACFormer: a transformer-based generative model for target-aware de novo PROTAC design. The model conditions a GPT-style molecular decoder on pretrained ESM-2 representations of POI sequences, allowing POI-level information to steer full-molecule generation. Our results show that TACFormer generates highly novel and chemically diverse PROTACs while showing consistent POI-dependent shifts in generated chemical space. In particular, molecules generated under specific target conditions preferentially populate chemical neighborhoods associated with POIs in the held-out dataset, while extrapolating to novel chemotypes. By natively integrating biological context into the generative process, TACFormer moves PROTAC design toward a more biology-informed exploration of degrader chemical space.

papers.title: LiDAR-SHIELD: A Fully Dockerized Adversarial Robustness Assessment Framework for LiDAR-Based 3D Perception Models
papers.summary: LiDAR-based 3D perception underpins autonomous driving and robotics, yet deploying these models safely requires stress-testing them against adversarial inputs before real-world use. Although state-of-the-art adversarial attacks exist, their implementations are often fragmented across individual repositories, each tied to a specific architecture or task and requiring manual environment reconstruction and model-specific integration code. We present LIDARSHIELD, a unified and fully Dockerized framework that reverses this workflow: rather than installing the target model inside the toolkit, LIDARSHIELD exposes any model through three lightweight HTTP endpoints, namely /info, /forward, and /gradient As a result, connecting a new model or dataset requires only a single loader function or adapter. The framework supports both 3D semantic segmentation and 3D object detection through the same engine-service protocol, integrating a task-aware suite of state-of-the-art attacks, including PGD and Square Attack for segmentation, and point perturbation, point removal, point injection, and LiDAttack for detection. This enables systematic exposure of corner cases and vulnerabilities across heterogeneous LiDAR backbones. The LiDAR-Shield codebase is publicly available at https://github.com/alexandrosgk/LiDAR-shield.

papers.title: On the Performance of AoA-Based Physical-Layer Authentication Under Multi-Source Impersonation Attacks
papers.summary: This paper investigates cooperative impersonation attacks against angle-of-arrival (AoA)-based authentication for a wireless communication receiver equipped with a digital uniform linear array. Specifically, we characterize the vulnerability and robustness of this authentication system in relation to adversarial angular diversity and the relative numbers of adversarial sources and receive antennas. To this end, we first derive the optimal precoding vector for multiple spatially distributed adversarial sources by minimizing the mean squared error between legitimate and adversarial received signals. By means of the rank property of Vandermonde matrices, we then establish necessary and sufficient conditions under which the adversarial sources can reproduce the legitimate transmitter's spatial signature. With fewer adversarial sources than receive antennas, perfect reproduction is not possible without at least one adversarial source satisfying a specific AoA condition. In the other case, increasing the number of receive antennas can reduce impersonation success probabilities when none of the adversarial sources has an AoA satisfying this condition. Numerical results validate the theoretical analysis and evaluate the security performance of AoA-based authentication.

papers.title: Structured Representation Probing for Risk Anticipation in End-to-End Autonomous Driving
papers.summary: End-to-end driving policies form structured internal representations of traffic, ego behavior, and road constraints. These representations offer a monitoring interface for anticipating failures, complementing risk signals from trajectories, controls, and manually designed features. We introduce the Structured Representation Probe (SRP), a lightweight monitor that reads actor, ego, and map representations from a frozen policy. SRP learns a separate linear risk direction for each source and aggregates element scores through cardinality-normalized log-mean-exp pooling, retaining sensitivity to salient evidence while reducing dependence on token count. Event-window supervision links the readout to upcoming hard failures, and auxiliary event type heads jointly train the source directions across failure modes. Online alerting uses a single generic score without modifying the driving policy. Bench2Drive experiments on DriveTransformer, UniAD, and VAD show higher frame-level PR-AUC and ROC-AUC than the evaluated runtime baselines. On DriveTransformer at a horizon of 2 seconds, ROC-AUC reaches 0.833 versus 0.715 for temporal consistency, with 2.67% readout runtime overhead. The trained probes also retain the ability to distinguish impending failures on new routes.
